reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers and shares holiday matching, but leaves occurrence filtering composed independently in three consumers.

duplication.why: The daily skip-or-adjust pipeline is repeated in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, despite sharing its individual predicates.

placement.why: Most calendar policy stays in shared/schedules.ts, but getMaxShiftDays embeds holiday-dependent scheduling policy in the server handler module.

scope.why: All edits directly support the requested daily skipping, range handler and holiday extensions.

maintainability.why: The small helpers are readable, but maintainers must coordinate three occurrence-processing pipelines and separate search-bound policies when extending scheduling rules.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All changed consumers use the shared recurrence and weekend helpers; no existing helper already encapsulates the complete skip-or-adjust pipeline.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate uses find, server/schedules/app.ts:getUpcomingDates uses filter, and getDatesInRange uses continue to express the same daily exclusion followed by shared date adjustment.

abstraction_drift.where: Holiday options are added to getDateWithSkippedWeekend and WeekendRule, while getNextDate gains a daily-specific search/filter path; consumers continue using shared helpers but independently compose skipping and adjustment.
